brief.answer: In 2025, the unemployment rate for young women (aged 15-29) in urban areas was 18.9%, about 7.1 percentage points higher than that of young men (11.8%). At the same time, only 23.2% of urban women aged 15-29 were in the labour force, compared with 60.9% of urban men of the same age group. The combination of a high unemployment rate and a very low labour‑force participation rate explains why many young urban women struggle to find work.

brief.answer: Unemployment is not rising in 2026; the latest monthly rate in September 2026 is 5.0%, which is 0.2 percentage points lower than September 2025. Monthly rates have hovered between 4.7% and 5.6% since April 2025, with no upward trend observed.
